title: t18190: Restrict needs-maintainer-review to external trust gates
body:
## What

Restrict `needs-maintainer-review` (NMR) to issues whose authors lack repository write authority. Trusted maintainer, collaborator, and framework-created issues must remain machine-actionable through normal claims, structural blockers, or circuit-breaker recovery instead of waiting for a maintainer to approve their own work.

## Why

The live queue currently contains 19 open NMR issues, 18 authored by OWNER or write-authorized actors. Creation paths can apply NMR immediately, worker checkpoint escalation adds it later, the triage workflow can silently fail to remove it under API pressure, and Pulse then preserves it as an intentional hold. This creates a self-review dead-end and stalls autonomous recovery.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** This changes an authorization boundary and must preserve circuit-breaker safety while removing false self-review gates.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`: normalize NMR at issue creation when creator trust is known.
- `.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate.yml`: make trusted-author normalization observable and fail closed on API failure.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh`: make author authority the invariant rather than label-actor provenance.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`: replace trusted worker checkpoint NMR with machine-recoverable state.
- `.agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh`: retain durable recovery without blind redispatch.
- `.github/workflows/nmr-hold-comment.yml` and `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml`: align hold and protection semantics where required.
- `.agents/AGENTS.md` and `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`: reserve NMR for external trust decisions and point other cases to structural blockers.
- Targeted shell and workflow regression tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`.

### Reference Pattern

Model authority checks on the repository-permission logic already used by `.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate.yml`, but make failure observable. Model machine-recoverable worker holds on the structural blocker labels documented in `.agents/reference/dispatch-blockers.md`; do not infer signed approval from write access.

### Complete Write Surface

Inspect every direct NMR add and remove path before editing. Change only paths needed to enforce the invariant end-to-end and document every intentionally retained external-author path.

### Implementation Steps

1. Centralize or reuse an authority check that distinguishes repository write authority from external authors and fails closed when authority cannot be established.
2. Strip or remove NMR for verified write-authorized authors without fabricating cryptographic approval. Preserve dependency, permission, infrastructure, blocked, `hold-for-review`, and `no-auto-dispatch` semantics.
3. Replace trusted worker and circuit-breaker NMR escalation with a machine-recoverable blocked or meta-repair route that cannot recreate the #19756 immediate retry loop.
4. Make triage cleanup failures visible so successful workflow status cannot conceal an unchanged trusted NMR gate.
5. Update guidance and regression tests, then reconcile the live queue after release.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- External non-writer issues must retain NMR until explicit trust approval.
- Unknown author authority must fail closed rather than weakening the trust boundary.
- Removing NMR must not imply signed approval or satisfy unrelated cryptographic gates.
- Circuit-breaker recovery must not blindly redispatch a failing worker.
- Existing machine-readable comments and labels should remain backward-compatible where practical.

### Verification Before Dispatch

Run targeted creation-wrapper, Pulse NMR, triage-gate, maintainer-gate, headless-worker, and circuit-breaker tests. Run ShellCheck and formatting checks for edited scripts, followed by `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`. Verify live GraphQL state after publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Verified OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, or write-authorized issue authors cannot remain blocked solely by NMR.
- [ ] External non-writer authors remain protected by NMR.
- [ ] API and rate-limit failures are observable and cannot be reported as successful normalization.
- [ ] Trusted circuit-breaker failures have a durable self-healing path without immediate retry loops.
- [ ] Regression tests cover creation-time, workflow-time, Pulse-time, and worker-checkpoint paths.
- [ ] After release, affected live issues are reconciled and only legitimate external trust gates retain NMR.

## PR Conventions

This is a leaf task; the implementation PR must use `Resolves #29394`.

## Brief Workflow

This issue follows `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. The implementation must preserve a complete write surface, explicit hazards, executable verification, and positive plus negative regression criteria.

title: bug(prrts): dead owner_dead_seen_at in worktree-registry.db causes silent worker launch failure + 1h cooldown lock
body:
## Description

When a PRRTS (pr-review-thread-response) worker is watchdog-killed, it leaves a registry entry in `worktree-registry.db` with `owner_dead_seen_at` populated. On the next dispatch attempt for the same PR, `_prrts_dispatch_worker` returns 0 (state file is written with `dispatched_at`), but the launched worker immediately exits silently — no lifecycle output, no metrics entry. The subsequent 3600s cooldown (`PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_COOLDOWN`) then locks out re-dispatch for 1 hour per attempt, compounding with repeated failures into indefinite lockout.

This caused all PRRTS dispatch attempts to fail silently for ~18 hours in a production session (all watchdog-killed workers from a previous cycle left dead owner records that blocked all subsequent PRRTS re-dispatch).

## Expected Behavior

When a PRRTS worker for PR `#N` is watchdog-killed and its worktree has `owner_dead_seen_at` set in `worktree-registry.db`, the next `_prrts_prepare_reused_worktree_owner` call should either:
1. Detect the dead-owner state and clear/re-claim the registry entry before launching, OR
2. Fail with a logged error and return `PRRTS_RC_RETRYABLE_FAILURE` (so state is NOT written with `dispatched_at` and cooldown is NOT triggered)

The worker must not return 0 from `_prrts_dispatch_worker` when the worktree ownership cannot be safely transferred.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: Any PRRTS `dispatch-pr` call after a watchdog-killed PRRTS worker for the same PR.

**Actual output**:

```
# Scanner log shows dispatch succeeded:
[2026-08-03T13:57:xx] dispatch: launched response worker for <owner>/<repo>#<N> in <worktrees>/<repo>-feature-auto-<date>-gh<N> pid=XXXX

# But NO lifecycle output follows — worker exits silently
# headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl: no entry for session pr-review-thread-response-<owner>-<repo>-<N>
# Pulse log: "review-thread remediation deferred — response dispatch active or recently deduplicated"

# Registry shows dead owner:
sqlite3 ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/worktree-registry.db \
  "SELECT worktree_path, owner_session, owner_pid, owner_dead_seen_at FROM worktree_owners WHERE owner_dead_seen_at != ''"
# Returns: <repo>-feature-auto-<date>-gh<N> | pr-review-thread-response-...-<N> | <pid> | 2026-08-03T12:14:22Z
```

**Expected output**: Either worker runs successfully, OR `_prrts_dispatch_worker` returns non-zero and `dispatched_at` is NOT written to state file.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation

**Suspected code path**:

- `_prrts_prepare_reused_worktree_owner` (`pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:1516`) reads dead owner via `_prrts_read_worktree_owner_snapshot`
- `_prrts_apply_expected_worktree_owner` (`pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:1435`) returns 0 (all fields populated, task matches)
- Sets `PRRTS_WORKTREE_TRANSFER_MODE=continuation` and `PRRTS_WORKTREE_EXPECTED_OWNER_PID=<dead_pid>`
- `setsid nohup headless-runtime-helper.sh run ...` launches (returns 0 immediately)
- State written with `dispatched_at` — **cooldown starts**
- Inside worker: suspected that `claim_worktree_owner` CAS in `shared-worktree-registry.sh` rejects transfer when `owner_dead_seen_at != ''`

**Call-site sweep**:
```bash
rg "_prrts_prepare_reused_worktree_owner|owner_dead_seen_at|claim_worktree_owner" .agents/scripts/
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch PRRTS workers (e.g. via `pr_review_thread_response` pulse stage)
2. Workers run for >600s and are watchdog-killed (`kill_reason=hard_kill_stall`)
3. Registry now has `owner_dead_seen_at` set for those worktrees
4. Attempt next PRRTS dispatch for the same PRs (state reset or next cycle)
5. Observe: scanner logs "launched response worker" but no lifecycle output, no metrics
6. Observe: 3600s cooldown locks out all subsequent attempts

## Workarounds Applied

The following manual interventions were required to unblock production:

1. **Registry cleanup** — remove dead owner records:
   ```bash
   sqlite3 ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/worktree-registry.db \
     "DELETE FROM worktree_owners WHERE owner_dead_seen_at != '' AND owner_session LIKE '%pr-review-thread-response%'"
   ```

2. **State file reset** — remove stale `dispatched_at` state to clear cooldown:
   ```bash
   rm ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/pr-review-thread-response/<owner>-<repo>-<PR>.state
   ```

3. **Manual dispatch** — directly invoke scanner after workaround:
   ```bash
   LOGFILE=/tmp/prrts-<PR>.log \
     pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh dispatch-pr <owner>/<repo> <repo_local_path> <PR>
   ```

**Systemic fixes needed**:
- `_prrts_prepare_reused_worktree_owner` should detect `owner_dead_seen_at` and clear the registry entry (or skip continuation mode)
- If ownership transfer will fail, `_prrts_dispatch_worker` must return non-zero **before** writing `dispatched_at` to state
- The 3600s cooldown (`PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_COOLDOWN`) should not activate when dispatch failed due to infrastructure (worktree ownership issue)

See-also: GH#29375 (related: silent PRRTS failure diagnostics gap post `post_worker_prepare`)

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.217
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0

## Additional Context

- ~18h of PRRTS lockout observed in production (all 12 open PRs in a managed repo were blocked)
- The root cause was a batch of watchdog-killed PRRTS workers from a previous cycle
- `dispatch_with_dedup` correctly logged "Preserving reused worktree until its expected continuation owner transfers" for these worktrees — the dispatch system was aware of the dead owners
- PRRTS scanner's `_prrts_prepare_reused_worktree_owner` does NOT check `owner_dead_seen_at` before proceeding with continuation transfer
- Only affected worktrees that were previously owned by PRRTS workers (not implementation workers)

title: bug(pulse-merge): CHANGES_REQUESTED gate unconditionally returns 1, blocking _attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry even when all threads converged
body:
## Description

`_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` in `pulse-merge.sh` always returns 1, blocking the entire downstream merge pipeline including `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry`. When a reviewer posts `CHANGES_REQUESTED` with the explicit instruction "Fix CI and request review again", pulse cannot auto-update the branch to fix CI drift — the reviewer is waiting for CI to go green, but pulse is waiting for the reviewer to approve first. Circular deadlock.

The affected path is `pulse-merge.sh:1523` (`_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry`), which is only reachable via `_check_pr_merge_gates` (line 1477), which is only reached after the CHANGES_REQUESTED gate (line 1436) returns 0. The gate never returns 0 for CHANGES_REQUESTED.

## Expected Behavior

When `_PULSE_MERGE_REMEDIATION_OUTCOME == "converged"` (all review threads resolved) AND the PR has terminal CI failures AND `mergeStateStatus == "BEHIND"` (branch is behind base), pulse should fall through to `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry` to update the branch. If the rebase fixes CI, the reviewer can re-evaluate and approve.

The gate comment at line 337 already notes: "no matching unresolved thread remained after refresh, preserving PR **for reevaluation**" — but no reevaluation ever happens.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
grep "CHANGES_REQUESTED\|rebase\|update.branch" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -20
```

**Actual output**:

```
[pulse-merge] review-thread remediation converged for PR #NNNN — no matching unresolved thread remained after CHANGES_REQUESTED review gate
[pulse-wrapper] Merge pass: skipping PR #NNNN — reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED; no matching unresolved thread remained after refresh, preserving PR for reevaluation
# _attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry never logged for this PR
# CI stays red, PR stays blocked, reviewer never re-reviews
```

**Expected output**: After "converged" + CI drift detected, `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry` runs and updates branch.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `pulse-merge.sh:1436` — `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate`
- **Call chain**: `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` → remediation "converged" → `return 1` (line 343) → caller `deterministic_merge_pass_pr` returns 1 → `_check_pr_merge_gates` (line 1477) never called → `_pr_required_checks_pass` never called → `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry` (line 1523) never called
- **Code gap**: `pulse-merge.sh:343` — `return 1` is unconditional regardless of remediation outcome

**Causal code**:

```bash
# pulse-merge.sh lines 336-343
elif [[ "$_PULSE_MERGE_REMEDIATION_OUTCOME" == "converged" ]]; then
    echo "...no matching unresolved thread remained..."
fi
return 1  # ← blocks ALL downstream paths including CI rebase retry
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Worker PR gets `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review with message "Fix CI and request review again"
2. Review threads are resolved (remediation converges)
3. PR branch is behind develop (drift)
4. Observe: pulse never runs `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry`, CI stays red
5. Manual fix: `gh pr update-branch <N>` → CI goes green → reviewer re-approves → merge

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually ran `gh pr update-branch` for PRs 3521, 3549, 3555, 3602, 3603 in Majowka/mesh-manager
- All 5 PRs showed `fails: []` immediately after update-branch (confirming pure drift, not code errors)

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.217
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0

## Additional Context

Related but distinct from GH#26045 (rebase-first prevents CI fix routing) — that issue was about rebase succeeding but CI routing being skipped. This issue is about rebase never being attempted at all because the CHANGES_REQUESTED gate exits unconditionally.

See-also: GH#29402 (dead owner registry blocks PRRTS dispatch)

title: bug(pulse-merge-feedback): legacy route marker at prior HEAD blocks re-routing after new commits — _feedback_route_review_generations_complete not used in prepare_start
body:
## Description

`_feedback_route_prepare_start` in `pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh` (line 288) holds a PR for maintainer review when the linked issue body contains a legacy route marker for the same PR at a different HEAD SHA. This permanently blocks `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` for any PR that has received new commits since its first routing pass, even after `review-routed-to-issue` label is removed.

The function checks: if `start_marker` (current HEAD) not in issue body, but `legacy_match` (any prior-HEAD marker for same PR) IS found → call `_feedback_route_hold_for_maintainer`. This means a PR that was routed at HEAD `abc` and then received new commits (HEAD `def`) can never be re-routed automatically — the old `<!-- feedback-route:start:review:PRN:SHAabc -->` marker triggers the hold.

## Expected Behavior

When a PR has received new commits since its last routing pass (HEAD changed), `_feedback_route_prepare_start` should check whether the prior generation was fully completed (start+completion marker pair exists). If the prior generation is complete, a new routing generation should be allowed for the current HEAD. `_feedback_route_review_generations_complete` appears to implement this check (line 101) but it is not invoked before the legacy marker hold at line 288.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
grep "legacy.*route\|head-bound\|no unambiguous" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -10
```

**Actual output**:

```
[pulse-wrapper] feedback finalizer: preserving PR #NNNN and issue #MMMM for maintainer review — legacy review terminal label has no unambiguous head-bound route evidence (issue_hold_rc=0, pr_hold_rc=0)
[pulse-wrapper] Merge pass: review feedback finalization for PR #NNNN requires maintainer review
```

**Expected output**: New routing generation starts for current HEAD SHA, PR is closed and issue re-dispatched.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `pulse-merge.sh:349` — `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` kind=review
- **Call chain**: `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` → `_dispatch_pr_fix_worker` → `_finalize_feedback_route` → `_feedback_route_prepare_start` (line 288) → `grep legacy_match in issue_body` → TRUE → `_feedback_route_hold_for_maintainer`
- **Causal code**: `pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh:285-291`

```bash
if printf '%s' "$issue_body" | grep -qF "$start_marker"; then
    return 0  # current HEAD already started → OK
fi
if printf '%s' "$issue_body" | grep -qF "$legacy_match"; then
    # OLD HEAD marker found → hold for maintainer
    _feedback_route_hold_for_maintainer ...
    return $?
fi
# _feedback_route_review_generations_complete is never called here
```

**Fix candidate**: Before line 288, call `_feedback_route_review_generations_complete "$issue_body" "$pr_number" "$start_marker"`. If it returns 0 (all prior generations complete), skip the legacy hold and proceed with new generation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Worker PR #N is routed to issue #M (adds `<!-- feedback-route:start:review:PRN:SHAabc -->` to issue body)
2. Worker pushes new commits to PR #N (HEAD changes from `abc` to `def`)
3. Remove `review-routed-to-issue` label from PR #N
4. Next pulse cycle: `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` called → `_feedback_route_prepare_start` runs → finds old SHA marker → holds for maintainer
5. PR stuck indefinitely — no new routing generation starts

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually closed PR #3412 via `gh pr close` to unblock issue #3407 re-dispatch
- Removing `needs-maintainer-review` and `review-routed-to-issue` labels alone was insufficient

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.217
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0

## Additional Context

Related but distinct from GH#29288 (ci-feedback-fallback + review-routed-to-issue dual-failure) — that issue covered the CI feedback path. This issue covers the review feedback path where a head SHA change after initial routing permanently blocks re-routing.

`_feedback_route_review_generations_complete` exists in the codebase and appears designed to detect complete prior generations, but is not used in `_feedback_route_prepare_start`.

See-also: GH#29402 (PRRTS dead owner registry), GH#<bug1-number> (CHANGES_REQUESTED blocks CI rebase)

title: bug(nmr): require explicit durable intent before creating review holds
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `trusted NMR false hold explicit intent auto-dispatch lifecycle preservation` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 9 recent commits / 0 merged search hits / 0 open search hits touched or matched the target surface; `e44975c97` and `f2970d04e` are relevant prior fixes, not duplicates
- [x] File refs verified: 8 refs checked against current `main`, all present
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — this corrects a dispatch trust-boundary classifier and live state migration
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the primary interactive session will implement after claiming a fresh linked worktree

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-08-03
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Production normalization translated trusted-author work into review holds merely because historical/shared-token NMR events lacked automation signatures. The maintainer clarified that issue creation is already implementation intent and human review is a last resort.

## What

Make trusted-author NMR normalization require explicit, durable unresolved-decision evidence before preserving or creating `hold-for-review`. Missing automation metadata, a write-authorized label actor, body prose, or historical NMR alone must not manufacture human intent. Preserve genuine external-author NMR, explicit reason/security gates, breaker recovery, and active lifecycle state.

Correct the currently observed false holds without disturbing parent-task, persistent tracker, active claim, or external-contributor semantics.

## Why

The current fallback converts clear `origin:interactive`, quality-debt, simplification, file-size-debt, and worker-created objectives into requests for reassurance. It consumed human attention, removed dispatch lifecycle labels, and stranded autonomous work. A generated `nmr-decision-packet reason=authority` is an output of the faulty classifier, not independent evidence of a human decision.

Repository-wide recent-comment evidence also shows repeated decision-packet comments on paginated issues, so the one-shot guard must flatten paginated results before counting markers.

## Reproducer

- **Symptom command**: `gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --state open --label hold-for-review --limit 100 --json number,author,labels,title`
- **Actual output**: 18 open trusted-author issues carried `hold-for-review`; their generated decision packets all used `reason=authority`, while clear implementation leaves had lost `status:available` and, in several cases, `auto-dispatch`.
- **Blocked command**: none; the normalization command completed successfully but produced semantically incorrect labels.
- **Backend state**: GitHub REST and GraphQL reads were healthy, and the issue timelines showed completed label mutations rather than a transport or API-budget failure.
- **Production entry point**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh` function `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` processes every open NMR issue during Pulse.
- **Call chain**: `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` → `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` → `_nmr_actor_event_is_manual_hold` → `_nmr_emit_decision_packet` and `_nmr_translate_trusted_author_hold`.
- **Integrated verification**: GitHub timeline, author-permission, current-label, and generated-comment queries showed write-authorized authors plus no structured reason/security evidence; the only inferred evidence was absence of an automation signature.
- **Causal status**: confirmed by the function branch at `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:1144-1166` and the production transitions observed on the same issues.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** The intended boundary is decided, but implementation touches live authority normalization, legacy breaker compatibility, lifecycle restoration, and a production backfill.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** A linked implementation worktree will be created immediately after issue claim.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Current source, tests, live labels, timelines, decision packets, and recent commits were inspected on 2026-08-03.
- **Verification run:** Discovery and live read-only classification completed; code tests not yet run.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Re-read live labels immediately before backfill because Pulse may change issue state concurrently.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `.agents/AGENTS.md` human-attention, task-lifecycle, and trust-boundary rules — preserve policy intent.
- **Then:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:1051-1276,1758-1926` — change reason classification, transition selection, lifecycle restoration, and packet idempotency.
- **Then:** `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh:176-267,397-418` — remove trusted NMR at creation rather than translating it into an implicit hold.
- **Stop after:** focused NMR/wrapper tests and affected documentation agree; do not broaden unrelated dispatch behavior.

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-maintainer-authority.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-nmr-normalization.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/auto-merge.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/task-lifecycle.md` or `.agents/reference/dispatch-blockers.md` only where wording still treats actor-only NMR as intentional

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh` functions `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer`, `_nmr_evaluate_reason_metadata`, and `auto_approve_maintainer_issues`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh` functions `_nmr_restore_dispatchable_state`, `_nmr_translate_trusted_author_hold`, and `_nmr_apply_auto_approval_transition`, plus `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh` function `_gh_ci_prepare_trusted_nmr_labels`.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-maintainer-authority.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh`, and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-nmr-normalization.sh`; update actor-only assumptions while retaining breaker, security, structured-reason, and external-author negatives.
- **Schemas/config:** existing `<!-- nmr-reason ... -->`, `hold-for-review`, `no-auto-dispatch`, `parent-task`, and `status:*` contracts; no new label required.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deploy occurs only through the normal post-merge setup/release path; do not edit `~/.aidevops/agents` directly.
- **Migrations/backfills:** use the GitHub issue timeline evidence to remove the 18 currently open false holds; restore `status:available` and `auto-dispatch` only for implementation leaves, preserve `#29387` active `status:in-review`, leave `#28659` structurally blocked by `parent-task`, and leave `#26416`, `#25313`, and `#24173` as persistent trackers.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** use `gh issue edit` against the recorded issue timeline to reverse label changes; revert the code PR and reapply only explicit holds if a regression is found.

### Implementation Steps

1. Replace actor-plus-missing-signature inference with explicit durable evidence. Structured reason markers, security labels, current explicit hold labels, and compatible breaker evidence remain authoritative; an unreasoned trusted-author NMR clears.
2. Make trusted cleanup preserve any existing `status:*` lifecycle label. Restore `status:available` only when status is missing, and do not add dispatch intent over explicit structural/manual blockers.
3. At trusted issue creation, remove a legacy NMR request instead of converting it to `hold-for-review`; callers that need a real internal decision hold must request `hold-for-review` explicitly. Preserve `external-contributor` and unverifiable-author NMR.
4. Flatten paginated decision-packet comments before the one-shot count to prevent repeated human-attention comments.
5. Hand-update focused regression tests and documentation.
6. Re-query live issue state, apply only the classified label corrections, and verify external NMR remains unchanged.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Pulse may mutate labels during backfill; re-fetch each issue immediately before editing and preserve active status/assignees.
- **Migration/rollback:** merge classifier tests before relying on future automatic cleanup; live false-hold removal can occur after implementation verification and is independently reversible.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** deployed older Pulse may reapply false holds until the fix is deployed. If no release is authorized, correct live labels at the end and record that recurrence remains possible until the next normal deployment.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated normalization must become a no-op; paginated decision packets must remain one-shot.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** report exact issues corrected and retry only failed mutations; never bulk-clear external NMR or security/breaker holds.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- **Surface mapping:** the four focused `bash` tests cover the NMR reader/writer and wrapper creation paths; `shellcheck` covers every touched shell file; `linters-local.sh --changed` covers repository integration.

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-maintainer-authority.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-nmr-normalization.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh \
  .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-maintainer-authority.sh \
  .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh \
  .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh \
  .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-nmr-normalization.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A trusted-author issue with unreasoned NMR and no explicit hold evidence loses NMR without receiving `hold-for-review` or a synthetic approval marker.
- [ ] A trusted wrapper-created issue requesting legacy NMR does not acquire an implicit review hold; explicit `hold-for-review` remains unchanged.
- [ ] External/unverifiable authors retain NMR; structured genuine-authority, security, and unresolved breaker evidence continue to gate.
- [ ] Trusted normalization preserves an existing active or blocked `status:*`; it creates `status:available` only when lifecycle status is absent.
- [ ] Paginated prior decision packets suppress duplicate comments.
- [ ] The 18 currently open false holds are corrected according to leaf/parent/persistent classification, while `#29387` and legitimate external NMR remain intact.

title: Fix task ID allocation blocked by pre-push repo verification
body:
## Task
Fix the task ID allocation path so claim-task-id.sh can update the task-id-counter branch even when local repo verification dependencies are missing or irrelevant to counter-only pushes.

## Why
Creating normal aidevops tasks is currently blocked. claim-task-id.sh must atomically push to refs/heads/task-id-counter before it can create a GitHub issue. In this session, task creation for Linux regression hardening failed twice: first with UNRECOVERABLE_COUNTER_DESYNC after CAS push timeouts, then with repeated push timeouts. Direct diagnosis showed the local pre-push hook blocks even a dry-run counter push before any remote update.

## Reproducer
From the aidevops worktree, run:

```bash
GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/task-id-counter
```

Observed output includes:

```text
[repo-verify][INFO] running typecheck: bun run typecheck
$ tsc --noEmit
/usr/bin/bash: line 1: tsc: command not found
[repo-verify][BLOCK] typecheck failed and autofix is unavailable.
error: failed to push some refs to github.com:marcusquinn/aidevops.git
```

This proves the counter push path is blocked locally by pre-push repo verification before remote CAS can complete.

## Evidence
- `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/task-id-counter refs/heads/main` succeeds and reports task-id-counter at 6cf50af179d5d4ab39187ce9532242457078e1b4, so remote read access is fine.
- `git fetch origin task-id-counter` succeeds.
- `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 -T git@github.com` authenticates as the current GitHub account.
- `git show origin/task-id-counter:.task-counter` shows 18191.

## How
### Files to Modify
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` and/or `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh` for the CAS push path.
- Pre-push hook/repo verification helpers under `.agents/scripts/` that decide when repo verification applies. Exact hook source should be discovered with `git ls-files .agents/scripts/*hook* .agents/scripts/*verify* .agents/scripts/*pre-push*`.
- Tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` for counter-only push behavior.

### Reference Pattern
Model the fix on existing scoped/skip logic in repo verification hooks: counter-only or metadata-only pushes should not require application typecheck dependencies. The dry-run failure shows the hook already detects `doc-only push`; extend the same concept to task counter CAS pushes instead of requiring full repo typecheck.

### Implementation Steps
1. Reproduce with the safe dry-run command above.
2. Identify which hook/helper emits `[repo-verify][INFO] running typecheck: bun run typecheck`.
3. Add a narrow bypass for task counter CAS pushes or counter-only changes. Do not disable hooks globally.
4. Ensure ordinary code pushes still run repo verification.
5. Add regression tests proving task counter pushes do not require `tsc` while code pushes still do.
6. After the fix, verify claim-task-id real task allocation no longer hangs on pre-push verification.

### Hazards and Compatibility
- Do not use `--no-verify` as the fix. The goal is a scoped hook policy for counter-only CAS pushes.
- Do not weaken code quality gates for real source changes.
- Keep behavior compatible with both OpenCode and Claude Code local hooks.

## What

## Reproducer

Run from current `main`:

```

The helper exits non-zero and prints an `Issue mentions` list that excludes `.agents/scripts/gh`, although issue #29049 names that exact path and PR #29136 changes it. Expected: exit zero with `.agents/scripts/gh (specific path match)`.

```

title: Scheduled auto-update ignores retention env overrides (only PATH injected into its LaunchAgent)
body:
## Summary

The documented storage-retention environment overrides for framework-owned stores take effect only in a process that inherits them. On macOS, the scheduled auto-update LaunchAgent injects **only `PATH`** into its environment, so background updates always prune with defaults (30 bundles / 8 GiB for `runtime-bundles`, 10 snapshots / 4 GiB for `agents-backups`). Operators who lower these limits see `~/.aidevops/runtime-bundles` and `~/.aidevops/agents-backups` drift back to the default ceilings on the next scheduled update, even though `reference/storage-lifecycle.md` presents them as operator-configurable.

## Affected knobs

- `AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_BUNDLE_MAX_COUNT`, `AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_BUNDLE_MAX_BYTES`, `AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_BUNDLE_RETENTION_SECONDS`
- `BACKUP_KEEP_COUNT`, `AIDEVOPS_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_DAYS`, `AIDEVOPS_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES`

## Evidence

- `reference/storage-lifecycle.md` → "Runtime Bundle Retention Overrides" documents these as overrides for "the update or setup process".
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh:913-915` — `_runtime_bundle_prune` reads the bundle limits from the environment.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/_backup.sh:7-9` — backup rotation reads `BACKUP_KEEP_COUNT` / `AIDEVOPS_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_DAYS` / `AIDEVOPS_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES` from the environment.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh:767-811` — `_build_plist_env_overrides_xml` already injects `~/.config/aidevops/plist-env-overrides.json` into the pulse / pulse-merge-routine / memory-pressure LaunchAgents.
- `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper-scheduler.sh:110-114` — the auto-update plist is generated with `EnvironmentVariables` containing only `PATH`; it never calls `_build_plist_env_overrides_xml`, so the override file is not consulted for the process that actually runs the retention prune.

## Impact

Retention overrides are effectively no-ops on the primary (background) update path. Users on small disks cannot durably lower the aidevops footprint without an out-of-band trimmer. In one install `~/.aidevops` sat at ~11 GB — 30 bundles (~7.1 GB) + 10 backups (~2.4 GB) — because the scheduled updater kept both at their default ceilings despite lower limits set in the operator's shell profile.

## Proposed fix

Have the auto-update LaunchAgent/systemd generator inject `plist-env-overrides.json` for its own label — call `_build_plist_env_overrides_xml "<auto-update-label>"` when composing `EnvironmentVariables`, matching the pulse / pulse-merge-routine / memory-pressure generators. A single `plist-env-overrides.json` entry keyed by the auto-update label would then durably apply the limits to scheduled updates.

Alternative: source the retention limits from `aidevops` config so all producers (setup, auto-update, pulse-triggered deploys) share one source of truth instead of relying on inherited environment.

## Suggested verification

- Add a test mirroring `.agents/scripts/tests/test-plist-env-overrides.sh` asserting the auto-update plist contains the injected keys when `plist-env-overrides.json` has an entry for the auto-update label.
- Manual: set `AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_BUNDLE_MAX_COUNT=3` in the override file, trigger a scheduled update, and confirm `runtime-bundles` converges to 3 + protected bundles.

# t18192: Pulse: refill all available worker slots immediately after worker exit

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `Pulse event-driven refill parallel full-loop claim release architecture implementation` → 0 hits; current-session evidence retained.
- [x] Discovery pass: recent dispatch changes reviewed; 0 merged or open PRs implement worker-exit-triggered refill.
- [x] File refs verified: lifecycle observer, wrapper mode dispatch, parallel capacity fill, and focused test surfaces exist at current HEAD.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — this changes the self-hosting dispatch path and concurrent scheduler state.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — runtime-safe coordination must be implemented and tested first.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-08-04
- **Session:** OpenCode interactive session for GH#29448
- **Created by:** AI DevOps (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** none; this is a leaf implementation issue.
- **Blocked by:** none.
- **Conversation context:** The user confirmed that Pulse must run several isolated `/full-loop` sessions in parallel, preserve claim/release comments, and continue through an aidevops release.

## What

Add a coalesced event-driven Pulse refill path. When a detached worker terminates,
signal Pulse immediately and fill every currently available local worker slot
through the existing parallel `dispatch_max` path. Keep the periodic Pulse cycle
as reconciliation fallback.

## Why

Production evidence on 2026-08-03 showed 24 configured slots, 21 free, two
eligible issues, and zero launches in 15 minutes. Worker execution was healthy
(14/15 terminal sessions reached runtime handoff), while initial dispatch
p50/p95 was about 324s/1548s and refill p95 about 1979s. The lifecycle observer
detects exits every five seconds but currently only appends a log line.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** The behavior is decided, but this is a high-risk scheduler
state-machine change in the self-hosting dispatch path. Concurrency, retry,
mixed-version, and crash-recovery behavior require runtime verification.

## PR Conventions

This is a leaf issue. The implementation PR uses `Resolves #29448`.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** A seed would anchor the worker before lock and trigger behavior is verified.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Memory, issue/PR discovery, recent commits, and file references checked against current HEAD.
- **Verification run:** Pre-edit and discovery checks only; implementation tests are not yet run.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Recheck the lifecycle observer and `dispatch_max` call path after any rebase touching Pulse dispatch files.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1283-1389`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1463-1516,1753-1905`, and `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:502-643` — these define the terminal event, wrapper mode, and parallel-fill boundaries.
- **Load only if:** `.agents/reference/cross-runner-coordination.md` when distributed claim behavior changes; `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` when lifecycle labels change.
- **Why:** The refill path must reuse existing authority and ownership gates instead of creating a direct-spawn scheduler.
- **Stop when:** one terminal event can safely request a full capacity refill without bypassing `dispatch_max` or GitHub claims.

### Worker Quick-Start

```bash
rg -n '_dlw_spawn_lifecycle_observer|worker_exited' .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh
rg -n '_pulse_setup_merge_only_mode|_pulse_run_merge_only|main\(\)' .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
rg -n 'dispatch_max\(\)|apply_dispatch_max' .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
```

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1283-1389` — publish a durable refill trigger after observing worker termination and invoke lightweight refill mode.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1463-1516,1753-1905` — recognize refill-only mode and drain pending triggers under the Pulse instance lock.
- `EDIT or NEW: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh:134-251` or a focused sourced helper — implement parsing, coalescing, lock-safe refill execution, and telemetry.
- `REFERENCE: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:502-643` — reuse existing parallel capacity fill; do not add a direct-spawn bypass.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh` — event, coalescing, full-deficit fill, stop-gate, and stale-trigger coverage.
- `EDIT: CHANGELOG.md` — record the user-visible throughput improvement under Unreleased.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` writes the trigger; `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` refill-only and normal Pulse paths drain it; operators read Pulse logs and stats.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` writes one machine-local trigger under the existing aidevops cache root; `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` removes it only while holding the Pulse instance lock. No repository or GitHub state is mutated directly by the trigger.
- **Dispatch lifecycle:** `dispatch_max` continues through `dispatch_with_dedup`, distributed claims, assignment/status updates, worker launch, release cleanup, and completion/blocker comments.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh`; existing wrapper characterization, worker-detection, minimum-concurrency, claim, and release tests remain regression coverage.
- **Schemas/config:** `N/A because` the trigger is presence-only disposable state; the environment escape hatch in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh` disables event refill while periodic scheduling remains active.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh --non-interactive` deploys `.agents/scripts/` only after the authorized release converges.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `N/A because` no durable schema is introduced; stale trigger state under the existing cache root is disposable and self-draining.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` drains stale triggers; disabling the event-refill gate or reverting the change restores timer-only behavior.

### Implementation Steps

1. Record a refill trigger before the lifecycle observer exits.
2. Invoke a lightweight `--refill-only` Pulse path that skips full preflight and LLM work.
3. Serialize refill against the main Pulse instance lock and coalesce simultaneous worker exits.
4. Drain the trigger and call existing `apply_dispatch_max`/`dispatch_max`, so one event can replace every missing worker within configured capacity and parallelism.
5. If a normal Pulse cycle owns the lock, retain the trigger and let that cycle drain it before expensive optional work or at its final deterministic refill boundary.
6. Preserve claim/release comments and status transitions by never bypassing `dispatch_with_dedup` or worker lifecycle cleanup.
7. Add structured trigger, refill, coalesced, disabled, and blocked telemetry with a safe environment escape hatch.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** simultaneous exits must not oversubscribe capacity or launch duplicate issues. Pulse lock ownership plus existing distributed GitHub claims remain mandatory.
- **Migration/rollback:** no migration. Disabling event refill immediately restores timer-only behavior.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** old workers omit triggers, so periodic scheduling remains fallback; new observers tolerate an older wrapper without refill mode.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated triggers may cause repeated capacity checks but never duplicate ownership. A trigger arriving during a refill remains pending for another pass.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** retain trigger evidence when lock acquisition or dispatch fails. Stop flags, provider/rate limits, runner health, trust, dependency, and circuit breakers still block launch.
- **Portability:** preserve Bash 3.2 and macOS/Linux behavior; do not introduce `flock` or `wait -n` outside existing compatibility wrappers.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Runtime verification:** terminate several fake detached workers, verify one coalesced trigger invokes the existing parallel dispatch path once, fills the full configured deficit, and does not directly spawn or bypass claim functions.
- **Surface mapping:** `test-pulse-event-refill.sh` covers trigger writers/readers and lock recovery; wrapper characterization covers CLI mode parsing; worker-detection and minimum-concurrency tests protect existing lifecycle and parallel-capacity dispatch.
- **Broad gate trigger:** shared Pulse and release-deployed shell paths change, so run the repository-required release preflight after focused checks.
- **Recoverability checkpoint:** create a WIP commit after focused runtime tests pass and before broad gates.

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** event-driven parallel refill with existing claim/release audit behavior.
- **Preserved user directions:** complete full-loop through merge, patch release, incremental deployment, and cleanup.
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** do not call worker launch directly from the lifecycle observer and do not bypass GitHub claim fencing.
- **Next safe route after a fuse:** keep the trigger pending, retain periodic fallback, reduce test concurrency, and resume from the WIP commit.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-bootstrap.sh` or one focused new sourced helper
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh`
- `CHANGELOG.md`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18192-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A worker terminal event requests refill without waiting for the 180-second scheduler interval.
- [ ] One refill pass targets all free slots through existing bounded parallel dispatch.
- [ ] Simultaneous exit events coalesce and cannot oversubscribe configured capacity.
- [ ] GitHub claim/release comments, assignment/status transitions, trust checks, dependency checks, and circuit breakers remain mandatory.
- [ ] A busy Pulse lock, stopped Pulse, unavailable GitHub, or disabled feature produces no unsafe launch and retains recoverable trigger evidence.
- [ ] Periodic Pulse scheduling remains a compatibility and crash-recovery fallback.
- [ ] Focused runtime, ShellCheck, changed-file, CI, review, release, publication, and deployment gates pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Keep persistent deterministic scheduler state separate from ephemeral per-issue LLM context.
- This leaf delivers event-driven capacity refill; revision-keyed ready projections and authoritative cross-runner campaign lanes remain separable future improvements.
- GitHub claims remain the distributed safety kernel and audit authority.
- Local terminal evidence may trigger scheduling immediately, but an issue cannot launch until its remote claim is confirmed.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none.
- **Blocks:** authoritative campaign dispatch and fleet-wide work stealing can build on this event path.
- **External:** existing Bash, GitHub CLI, jq, and local scheduler services; no new dependency or secret.
